newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Just Jeans shares drop to 34-month low.
newsitem.headline: Just Jeans shares drop to 34-month low.

text.p: Shares in jeans retailer Just Jeans Holdings Ltd fell 12 cents or about 7.4 percent to A$1.50, their lowest level since October 1993, following a profit warning after the close of trading on Monday.
The company said pre-tax profit would be 65 percent lower in the year to end-July than in the previous corresponding period.
Just Jeans cited poor merchandise decisions combined with exceptionally difficult apparel retailing conditions for the slump in earnings.
"It's on the back of the announcement. That is the only news on the stock," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.

Just Jeans' reported net profit rose to A$14.11 million in the year to July 27, 1996, from A$12.65 million in 1994/95. The group reported a 48.9 percent fall in net profit to A$4.63 million for the six months ended January 25, 1997.
By 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), Just Jeans had recovered some ground to be seven cents lower at A$1.55 on turnover of 59,310 shares.
